questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted a well performing school in a city with cultural relevance. 
I wanted a city were it was possible easily to travel around. 
Also, a city whit equality in the community and open minded people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was kind of hard to figure out information about if I have gotten the classes that i replied for. 
I just showed up in class without any knowledge about that I was accepted.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received information on were to get my erasmus studentcard.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
I general Erasmus students needs more information about the classes. 
I did not get information on which classes I was accepted in. 
I did not get information about were they would take place and when. 

I think that Erasmus people needs a guide to the University of Milans platforms such as Unima and Ariel. Both of the websites are quite hard to figure out.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I did it through AirBnB. I was early finding it, so I think that I was lucky. I heard a lot of people struggling and paying a lot for their rooms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Find a place within the "circle" around the city. 
Here it will be easy for you to get around by walk, with metro, train, tramps and so on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied by the fact that I found my own apartment.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The italian system is quite confusing and you dont get confirmations on your actions.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The process was fine to register at the University. 
But it was kind of hard with the classes and no notice about confirmation/redjection.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could write the erasmus team on the school.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I just showed up in the classes I replied for, without knowing that I was registred.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write the Erasmus team from the University of Milan. That is the best help you can get.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
One of my courses 'Social and Political Attitudes' were really different from the desciption. 
It was required to have statistical skills, which is not informed on the class description. 
I had a hard time following the class because of the missing information about the content of the academic program.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I was a BA in Denmark, but did Master classes. 
I did that because I could not get any classes on english at BA level within my field.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very different. 

In both of my classes we used the hours of the teaching classes to do exames - also in front of the whole class. 
In one of my classes we had 6 weeks of teaching program and 6 weeks of presentations (exams) from the students. I found that really odd. 

Furthermore, both classes both had written and oral exams, though it is written on the course description that there are only one exam in each. It seem like that the teachers choose themself how they wants to examines. In addition, there was no censors during the exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 'Datafied Society' and 'Social and Political Attitudes'

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I liked Datafied Society. 

It is really relevant class with the newest theories about data, algorithms, social media platforms and issues around these themes. It is really relevant for people who are interested in communication and marketing.

questions.answer: Non

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Fitness is really expensive in Milan. 
I paid 3000 DKK for 6 month (including student discount)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not do that many - I think there were too many people and too little control of it. And they did really touristy things.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything. They both has tennis and football competitions, City tours and parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The first gathering of Erasmus people. Here you can meet new people which is in the same situation as you.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit other cities. It is very easy to travel by train from Milan. 
You can go all over Italy. 
It gets really warm from May, and around 35 degrees in June. Here I would recommend to go to the seaside or to Lake Como which is only 40 minutes away by train and cost 5 euros.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
It was really easy. 
Milan is a big city like Copenhagen, the culture is a bit different, but people are very welcoming and much more openminded compared to danish people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just visit a lot of bars or go to the University parks. Dont worry, people will reach out to you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
They eat really late - be prepared for that. Restaurents opens around 7.30. 
They are still a bit traditional and the men has more power than women.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That Italians are really openminded and always reach out to strangers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The University system is very different from KU. But dont worry, there is nothing wrong about you not getting answers or information. You just show up and you will figure it out. They are not so structured. 

2. The classes are not necessary the same as you expected at all. 

3. Be prepared for the heat. It is really hot in June/July with no wind and no sea-side.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Milan is huge, so just walk around the beautiful city and get lost in the nice and old historical buildings.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social life - to get to know italian people and the culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Understanding their structure - They are way more "loose" than danish people. Anything will be fine in their opinions, no stress is needed.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
